title: The globe as an imperial and cosmic stage
grounded_significance: Jahangir’s allegories place the ruler on a mapped sphere and subordinate other beings or rulers through scale and position. distinctions: These are visual claims to authority, not photographs of real meetings, military victories or literal positions in space.

title: Engraving and intaglio
grounded_significance: In engraving, cut lines in a plate retain ink for transfer to paper. It is an intaglio process, distinct from raised-surface printing. A work can circulate through impressions while its design is adapted into another medium.
distinctions: Engraving is not the general name for all prints; woodcuts and lithographs use different printing principles.

title: Inlay versus incision
grounded_significance: Inlay inserts a contrasting material into a prepared ground. Bidri provides a documented metalwork example in this course. A visible colour contrast is a starting observation; close inspection or a catalogue is needed to distinguish inserted metal from applied paint or shallow engraving.
distinctions: Inlay adds a material to prepared recesses; engraving cuts a surface without necessarily inserting another material.

title: Iwan and courtyard organization
grounded_significance: An iwan is a vaulted space open on one side, often addressing a courtyard. The madrasa comparisons invite attention to the large framed opening, its depth and the court it serves, rather than simply treating it as a tall doorway.

title: Japonisme: reception and transformation

title: Reproducibility and production scale

title: Mordant and resist dyeing
grounded_significance: A mordant helps selected dyes bind to cloth; a resist prevents colour reaching protected areas. Both can participate in a multistage textile process. The distinction concerns how colour is fixed or excluded, not simply whether the finished cloth has red and blue areas.
distinctions: Mordant and resist are complementary operations, not synonyms for the same chemical action.

title: Porcelain and cross-medium comparison

distinctions: White ground and blue decoration alone do not establish porcelain, Chinese manufacture or a particular trade route.

title: Pronk and sumptuous display
grounded_significance: Pronk still life emphasizes sumptuous objects and conspicuous abundance. Reflective vessels, costly foods and imported wares can demonstrate pictorial skill while evoking wealth and circulation. distinctions: Pronk describes ostentatious display; it is not a synonym for every still life or a specific pigment technique.

title: Registration and misregistration
grounded_significance: Registration aligns successive printed elements. Ukiyo-e colour production used alignment guides for its blocks. Misregistration is an offset between intended positions; a coloured contour must be examined before calling it a defect. No accidental misregistration is securely demonstrated in the supplied lecture impressions.
distinctions: Registration is an alignment operation, not a printing medium; misregistration cannot be inferred simply from visible outlines.

title: Relief printing
grounded_significance: In relief printing the inked raised surface prints while cut-away areas remain unprinted. Woodblock prints are a central example. The image is multiplied through a matrix, unlike a carved architectural relief that remains on its original support.
distinctions: Relief print and sculptural relief share a word but have different functions and image-making sequences.

title: Yali and composite animal forms
grounded_significance: Museum accounts describe yali forms through combinations of lion, elephant or horse-like features and their use in southern architecture. Individual specimens vary. distinctions: A yali is not a natural zoological species, and every composite creature is not necessarily the same mythological being.
